**Reading map:** Deisenroth, Faisal & Ong, *Mathematics for Machine Learning* (2020), §3.3. This is an original lesson using our delivery-operations example—not reproduced textbook content.

## Why the concept matters

A delivery order's location in feature space changes as distance or item count changes. A metric gives a formal meaning to nearby and far apart.

## Define the mathematical relationship

$$
d(\boldsymbol x,\boldsymbol z)=\|\boldsymbol x-\boldsymbol z\|_2
$$

The displayed relationship is the main object to analyse. Specify the relevant dimensions, quantities and assumptions before using it. It should be read as a mathematical statement, not merely a programming shorthand.

## Work through an original example

Compare x=(2,1) and z=(5,3): the difference is (-3,-2) and the Euclidean distance is sqrt(13), approximately 3.606. If both coordinates represent unrelated units, this numerical distance needs interpretation.

## What follows, and what does not

Distance is nonnegative, symmetric and satisfies the triangle inequality. Squared Euclidean distance is convenient in optimisation but is not itself a metric in general.

## Test your reasoning

Why does doubling one coordinate's measurement unit change Euclidean distances?
